ad17_families.topic: Families through the machine: BLS CE 2024 quintile budgets, history 2020-2024, CE definitions, SCF 2025 by income percentile, shocks

claims.text: BLS CE income before taxes (USD per consumer unit) 2020-2024: lowest fifth 13,219; 13,165; 14,191; 15,596; 16,658. Total average annual expenditures lowest fifth 28,732; 30,869; 32,618; 33,776; 35,046.

BLS CE second fifth (21st-40th percentile) income before taxes 2019-2024: 32,768; 34,550; 34,767; 37,441; 40,751; 42,925. Total expenditures 2020-2024: 39,899; 43,918; 47,665; 48,923; 50,054. Age of reference person 55.1 (2021), 55.2, 55.8, 56.0 (2024). 2024 healthcare 4,826 (2023 4,844); personal insurance and pensions 2,712; transportation 8,430.

BLS 2024 release: unable to produce federal and state tax estimates or after-tax income for 2024 (tax model provider did not update); quintiles formed by sorting consumer units by income before taxes, about 27 million units each; lower bounds second $29,932, third $57,452, fourth $94,511, highest $155,925; all units personal insurance and pensions $9,797 incl. deductions for Social Security $6,684 and contributions to retirement plans $1,991; CE income includes wages, self-employment, Social Security and retirement, interest, dividends, rent, unemployment benefits, public assistance and other income.

BLS CE glossary: expenditures are transaction costs including excise and sales taxes; periodic credit or installment payments on goods already acquired are excluded; owned dwellings include mortgage interest, home equity interest, property taxes and insurance; mortgage principal 'is not included in homeowner costs but is repayment of a loan'; vehicle purchases are net outlay; vehicle finance charges are interest on vehicle loans; income after taxes = income before taxes less federal, state and local income and other personal taxes; earner = member 14+ who worked at least one week in the past 12 months; consumer unit = family, financially independent single person, or persons sharing major expenses.

SCF 2025 (thousands of 2025 dollars, CPI-U-RS; families grouped by percentile of USUAL income): median income <20th pct 24.6, 20-39.9 50.5, 40-59.9 83.1, 60-79.9 129.2, 80-89.9 201.3, 90-100 387.2. Median net worth 2025 (2022): <20 14.4 (15.3); 20-39.9 77.1 (77.7); 40-59.9 188.2 (174.4); 60-79.9 362.5 (336.1); 80-89.9 814.6 (817.5); 90-100 3,669.9 (2,797.5). All families: 77.0% have debt, conditional median debt $88.1k, median payment-to-income ratio for debtors 15.4%, 8.6% with payments above 40% of income, 8.2% 60+ days late; transaction accounts median among holders $8.2k; upper-middle income group homeownership 80% to 78%, top decile 89% to 92% (Box 4).

Book arithmetic from BLS CE (income before taxes minus total expenditures, % of income), 2020-2024: lowest fifth -117.4, -134.5, -129.8, -116.6, -110.4; second -15.5, -26.3, -27.3, -20.1, -16.6; middle 13.2, 8.7, 5.6, 7.8, 10.2; fourth 26.0, 25.1, 24.6, 24.7, 26.0. 2024 after-tax estimate (2023 income-tax ratios 6.26%/10.42% plus 7.65%/15.3% payroll): middle fifth taxes $9,412 (12.6%), spending excl. personal insurance and pensions $60,652, left $4,410 (5.9%), of which ~$1,500 private pensions/life insurance; fourth fifth taxes $21,222 (17.5%), spending $78,038, left $22,288 (18.3%).

ad17_life.topic: A life in numbers: first-job earnings, rent and first-home prices, out-of-pocket limits

claims.text: BLS Q3 2026 (not seasonally adjusted) median usual weekly earnings of full-time wage and salary workers: 16-19 $682; 20-24 $802; 25-34 $1,173; 35-44 $1,414; 45-54 $1,407; 55-64 $1,376; 65+ $1,165. Book arithmetic x52: 20-24 $41,704; 25-34 $60,996; 35-44 $73,528.

Census HVS Q2 2026 (released 28 July 2026): homeownership 65.0% (65.0% Q2 2025); rental vacancy 7.3%; median asking rent for vacant for-rent units $1,531; median asking sales price for vacant for-sale units $343,800; homeownership under 35 35.2% (36.4% Q2 2025, the only age group with a significant fall), 35-44 60.9%, 45-54 69.7%, 55-64 75.1%, 65+ 78.6%.

HealthCare.gov: 2026 Marketplace out-of-pocket maximum $10,600 individual, $21,200 family; 2027 $12,000 / $24,000; premiums, non-covered services, out-of-network care and balance bills do not count toward it.
